resources.string: Blockfy uses Accessibility to leave short-video screens and, with adult blocking on, to check the address bar of your browser against a list of adult sites. It does not read messages, chats, or anything you type in other apps, and does not save what it reads.

Blockfy only works with Accessibility turned on. It uses this permission to detect and leave short-video screens (Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, X) and to count time in those apps. If you turn on adult blocking, it also reads your browser\'s address bar to check the site you are visiting against a list of adult sites. It never reads messages, chats, passwords, or anything typed inside other apps, and does not save or send what it reads. Blockfy does not open banking apps. By tapping Accept you agree to this use.

1. Open app info and allow restricted settings, if the phone asks.
2. Open Accessibility settings.
3. Under downloaded apps, tap Blockfy.
4. Turn the service on and confirm.
On some phones you must first allow restricted settings from the Blockfy app info screen.
Brazil uses Portuguese. Everywhere else uses English, until you change it here.

Blockfy pulls you out of Reels, Shorts, and feeds like that. You can set a daily limit. Adult blocking, if you turn it on, uses Accessibility to check your browser\'s address bar against a list of adult sites. It does not use a VPN.\n\nRobin Gebert made the original, Blokky. Samuel Bueno keeps this fork going. It is still a small short-video blocker.

Accessibility watches Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and X to detect short videos. With adult blocking on, it also reads your browser's address bar to check it against a list of adult sites; it never reads messages, chats or anything typed in other apps, and does not save what it reads. It does not open banking apps and does not use a VPN.

Updates should come from Google Play. Blockfy does not install APKs by itself.

If you find this app useful, you can support it on GitHub: https://github.com/buenotty/Blockfy

resources.string: A reminder of why these blocks exist, for the day you feel like turning them off.
What the feed does to your attention, your work and your mood.
What it costs your character, your relationships and your sex life.

string-array.name: concept_shorts_titles
string-array.item: Your work gets thinner
Dopamine stops waiting
It is built to be endless
Sleep and mood pay the bill
Other people start to look small

string-array.name: concept_shorts_bodies
string-array.item: A few minutes becomes an hour because each video ends before your brain decides to stop. The task you opened the phone to do is still waiting, and starting it feels heavier than it did before.
Short videos train you to expect a hit every few seconds. Ordinary work, conversation and silence start to feel dull, not because they got worse, but because your reward system got louder.
There is no last episode. The next one is already loaded, picked because it is more likely to keep you there. The product is your time, not the video.
Late scrolling steals the sleep that would have made tomorrow easier. You wake up more irritable, less patient, and more likely to open the same app again.
A feed of other people\'s highlights makes your own day look like a failure. That comparison is not information. It is a side effect of watching strangers perform.

string-array.name: concept_porn_titles
string-array.item: It trains you to use people
Your character erodes in private
Relationships get colder
Your sex life shrinks
You can leave

string-array.name: concept_porn_bodies
string-array.item: Pornography teaches you to treat another person as a product: available, silent, and discarded when the feeling passes. That habit does not stay on the screen. It shows up in how you look at people who are actually in the room.
Doing this in secret splits you in two. You say one thing about who you are and keep another life that you would not defend out loud. Character is what you repeat when nobody is scoring you.

A partner is not a stream of novelty. If your arousal depends on strangers, tabs and escalation, the person who loves you starts to feel insufficient. That is not their failure. It is the cost of the habit.

Heavy use makes real intimacy slower, more anxious, or harder to enjoy. You need more intensity for the same effect, and an ordinary body next to you stops being enough. That is a damaged appetite, not a high standard.

You will find a way around a block if you are determined. The point of the block is the pause: long enough to remember that this does not give you a better life, a clearer mind, or a relationship you can respect.
